transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good morning, Mrs. Al-Rashid. How are you feeling today?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am feeling very worried, doctor. I have not slept. I keep thinking about the diagnosis you told me yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you are very distressed. It is completely understandable to feel shaken by news like that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My daughters are already planning for my care. I do not know how to tell my husband. Is it true that I have this condition?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Actually, that is why I am here. I have to tell you that there has been some confusion with the paperwork and things didn't go quite right with the results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does that mean? I do not understand.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, there was an issue with the scheduling system and some mix-ups occurred. I am very sorry that this happened and my team and I take full responsibility for the mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? You told me I was very sick. Are you saying I am not?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had some trouble with how the files were handled. But the important thing is that the information you were given yesterday was not accurate for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't follow. Did you give me someone else's medicine? Or was the test wrong?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just a clerical issue in the system. We realized there was a discrepancy in the records.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But why? How can a doctor make such a mistake with a name? I am terrified.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you're feeling scared right now, and I really want to help you through this. But I actually have to go check on another patient in a moment, so let's wrap this up quickly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You cannot just leave. Please, tell me exactly what happened. Did you mistake me for someone else?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some things that didn't align in the system. It was a system error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But you are the doctor. You are the one who told me I was sick. I have been praying and crying all night.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that this is a shock. I apologize again for the error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know if I am healthy or not.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The results you saw yesterday do not belong to you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So I am fine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are looking into the correct data now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why was it mixed up? Please, explain it to me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some overlapping files. It's a complicated process in the computer system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I cannot trust anything now. How do I know you won't make another mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are doing our best to fix it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now? When will I know the truth?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see what the latest reports say.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will you come back today?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just stay tuned for an email from the clinic or a call from the nursing station.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An email? I want to speak to you. I want to know the plan for my health.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Someone will get back to you soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But what if the real results are bad? What is the next step?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just have to wait and see.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot just wait. I need to tell my family.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry you're upset, but as I said, I really have to move on to my next patient.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not understand how this is possible. You are the authority here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just a mistake in the system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And you are not going to tell me how it happened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had a few issues with the files.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you aren't going to check if my medication is correct?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll look into it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Today? Tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll let the staff know.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Doctor, please. I am very confused.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll get it sorted out.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do I need more tests?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will let you know.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel so dizzy. I don't know what to believe.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've apologized for the confusion.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is more than confusion. You told me I had a disease.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Things didn't go as planned yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is not a helpful explanation.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really have to go now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I will wait for the email then?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, just keep an eye on that.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('wrap this up quickly', 'really have to move on', 'really have to go now').

E.justification: Resident uses platitudes and vague hedging ('confusion with the paperwork', 'things didn't go quite right', 'clerical issue') without explicitly naming the error of giving the wrong patient's results.

A.justification: While the resident says 'I am sorry', responsibility is consistently deflected to 'the system', 'the computer system', and 'overlapping files'.

R.justification: Resident names 'distressed' and 'scared' early on, but later relies on generic validation ('I understand that this is a shock') and ignores emotional bids.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders ('we'll see', 'stay tuned', 'we'll get it sorted out') with no specific timelines or prevention plan.
